messages:
maria: Heads-up — ACME asked for a p99 tail-latency guarantee for Dedicated pools. Their calls are sensitive to cold KV/prefix cache misses which spike tail latencies during sudden surges. sales already asked if we can promise <250ms p99 for most traffic.
ashok: short answer: maybe. We can reduce cache-miss tails with pre-warmed micro-pools + slower eviction for KV caches, but it costs GPU hours and complexity. Need concrete config / SLO tradeoffs. :thinking:
emily: what do you mean by slower eviction? if we hold cache state across scale-in that's more memory and bookkeeping for the runtime. also affects packer/autoscaler logic.
jonathan: proposing a concrete MVP config so we can scope rollout and pricing. idea: reserved_pools.prewarm_enabled=true, prewarm_replicas=2 per pool, kv_cache_grace_ttl=600s, prefix_cache_threshold=0.6 (keep if >=60% warm). That should blunt cold tails for short bursts.
ashok: that config is doable. runtime changes: 1) mark prewarm nodes that do not accept user load until warmed, 2) when scale-in, mark nodes as "drain+cache-retain" for kv_cache_grace_ttl, evict only after TTL, 3) expose cache_warmth metric per-pool. I'll sketch patches.
emily: two operational asks: add a drain window to autoscaler (so scale-in doesn't instantly remove warmed slots) and an alert when pool cache_warmth < 0.5 for >5m. Without that we might silently regress.
sales_amy: ACME will pay for a small uplift if we can demonstrate stable tails in a pilot. Need pilot acceptance criteria: what are we measuring?
cust-success-ben: suggested pilot plan: 2-week pilot on a reserved pool (their production tenant), start with traffic shadowing + then cut 10% of live traffic, validate: 1) p99 latency <250ms for 95% of calls; 2) tail-spike events (p99 >500ms) <= 1 per day; 3) total monthly cost delta <= 15% vs their current baseline. If all pass, convert to rollout.
maria: we should tighten the cost delta to <=12% for internal launch criteria. Also require we have metrics surfaced in Console: cache_warmth, prewarm_node_util, p99_by_route, and an incident runbook for regressions.
jonathan: rollout plan draft: stage 1 (internal): enable prewarm on a small internal pool + synthetic burst tests; stage 2 (pilot): ACME 2-week pilot; stage 3 (beta): open to customers on dedicated; stage 4 (GA) with pricing uplift and SLA language. Each stage gated by runbook ops play, cost/latency thresholds, and e2e integration tests.
nashok: implementation notes: code changes in runtime to add cache retention on scale-in, new autoscaler flag scale_in_grace_seconds, metric cache_warmth = fraction of KV keys with hotness>threshold. We'll need a DB migration to persist prewarm annotations and a small API change to control per-pool prewarm count.
emily: add ops checklist: add SLO dashboards, alert on prewarm_failures, ensure node labeling for prewarm workloads, document rollback (disable prewarm flag + immediate forced eviction).
sales_amy: who's owning pricing language? We need a SKU: "Reserved pool prewarm add-on" with % uplift. Can we model cost impact for ACME pilot? finance to run numbers once eng gives rough GPU-hours.
maria: action items: @ashok send RFC w/ config/options by EOD Friday; @emily add ops checklist and example dashboards; @jonathan write pilot acceptance doc and telemetry queries; @sales_amy get ACME commitment for 2-week pilot. I'll own cross-team kickoff.
ashok: RFC note: default values I propose: prewarm_replicas=2, scale_in_grace_seconds=600, kv_cache_warmth_threshold=0.6, prewarm_cpu/share_lim=low. We'll run perf sims to estimate cost.
cust-success-ben: for pilot we'll provide load patterns (burst shapes). We'll also arrange a run with our chaos agent to simulate rapid spikes.
deploy-bot: infra-ticket created: #INFRA-8473 (prewarm annotations + scale_in_grace config).
maria: thanks — next sync Tue 10am. :+1:
